whatItDoes: Turns one blog post or transcript into a tweet thread, LinkedIn post, newsletter section, quote graphics, and a short clip, then emails the pack to everyone on your list. Runs on a schedule against your latest post, or set `dryRun` to read the copy before anything is generated.
longDescription: Give it one blog post or transcript and it hands you a whole content pack: a tweet thread, a LinkedIn post, a newsletter section, quote graphics, and a short teaser clip. A model (`llm.run`) rewrites the source into every channel at once, keeping your meaning instead of inventing claims. It makes the media one job at a time, gathers everything into a markdown pack, saves it, and emails it to each recipient on your `deliverTo` list. Set `dryRun` to stop after writing the copy.
notes:
Click **Use this template**. Sapiom builds and deploys it for you; open it on the **Agents** page and run it.

`source` is the only required input. Paste the blog post or transcript text. Set `dryRun: true` to stop after writing the copy and read it before any images or video are generated. Keep `numQuotes` small (default 2, max 4). Set `renderClip: false` to keep the quote graphics but skip the teaser clip, the priciest, slowest leg. To have it email the pack, set `deliverTo` to one or more addresses; the pack fans out, one send per recipient. Without it the run returns the pack and sends nothing. Give it a `schedule` (a cron string) to run it as a standing job.

Prefer to work from the code? Run it locally with `run_local` and `{ "dryRun": true }` to trace the copy step, or edit and deploy it with the Sapiom MCP.
